name: BRISCOLA
description: Briscola is Italy's most beloved card game, a point-trick game played with the distinctive 40-card Italian deck (suits: coins, cups, batons, swords). Each player holds 3 cards and draws after each trick. The trump suit is revealed by the last card dealt, which stays visible until taken. The unusual ranking system (Ace > 3 > King > Queen > Jack > 7-2 in point order) makes Briscola distinct from virtually every other card game in the world.

content.text: Briscola is Italy's most beloved card game, a point-trick game played with the distinctive 40-card Italian deck (suits: coins, cups, batons, swords). Each player holds 3 cards and draws after each trick. The trump suit is revealed by the last card dealt, which stays visible until taken. The unusual ranking system (Ace > 3 > King > Queen > Jack > 7-2 in point order) makes Briscola distinct from virtually every other card game in the world.
Briscola developed in Italy from older European Ace-Ten card games. The word 'briscola' means trump in Italian. The game is one of the founding pillars of Mediterranean card culture.
Score 61 or more of the 120 available card points.

Each trick: non-dealer leads any card. No follow-suit obligation. Opponent plays any card. Trick won by higher Briscola (trump) played, OR higher of led suit if no Briscola. Winner draws first from stock; loser draws second. Winner leads next. Final trick: trump indicator card is last taken from stock.

items.text: Trump (Briscola) beats all off-suit cards regardless of rank.
The trump-indicator card is taken by the winner of the last draw-phase trick.
Pointing cards: only A, 3, K, Q, J have value.

content.text: Lead worthless cards (7-2) to bait opponents into spending Aces or 3s on nothing-tricks.
Trump Economy: Don't trump low-value tricks. Save your Briscola Ace for the opponent's Ace-led trick.

End-of-Stock Timing: Once the stock depletes, you know both hands. Calculate exactly who has which trump card. A Briscola 3 in hand is a second-place trumpâ€”use it to steal the opponent's 7 so they can't counter your Briscola Ace.
First to 61 card points wins the deal.
